title: Zephyrine and the Safehouse
premise: Emrys Pemberton has spent six years laundering his own past into a spotless life as a compliance investigator, keeping a go-bag by the door for the day someone finds him. When a woman named Zephyrine arrives claiming he once saved her life in Marseille—a favor he has no memory of, because it never happened—she demands repayment: help her stop a staged industrial 'accident' that will launder a fortune and bury a whistleblower. Emrys must choose between running as his instincts demand and staying to uncover why his fabricated memories and her real ones overlap. In the end he exposes the plot, loses the safehouse identity he built, and leaves on the dawn flight not as a fugitive but as himself, with Zephyrine beside him and his memory finally his own.
about_author: Vesper Galloway is the pen name of a former financial journalist who spent a decade reporting on offshore fraud before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town whose location they decline to confirm, and all their thrillers begin with the same question: what would you do to stay forgotten?

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A meticulous morning routine reveals his double life: flawless compliance investigator by day, man with a packed bag and three exit routes by night. A routine audit flags an anomaly he can't explain. Beat: controlled unease—the lie is polished, but it's starting to crack.

chapters.title: A Favor Returned
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Zephyrine appears at his office claiming he pulled her from a burning safehouse in Marseille six years ago, and that her debt is now due. He has no memory of it—and worse, the details match a night he's erased from his own records. Beat: vertigo; the past he invented is colliding with one that's real.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Zephyrine explains the repayment: help her stop a chemical plant 'accident' scheduled in nine days, engineered to kill a whistleblower and launder €40 million through insurance. Emrys refuses and goes home to find his apartment searched—professionally, by someone who knew where the go-bag was. Beat: refusal collapses into entrapment.

chapters.title: The Clean Money
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She traces the money trail through shell companies and recognizes Emrys's own signature techniques in the laundering structure—someone taught the conspirators his methods. Beat: her suspicion that Emrys is a plant, not a savior, hardens even as she needs him.

chapters.title: Marseille, or Something Like It
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He digs into his own sealed files and finds a Marseille hotel receipt he cannot account for, dated the night of Zephyrine's fire. His mentor Aldous Vane, retired, warns him to take the go-bag and disappear. Beat: the temptation to run versus the need to know.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He agrees to help—not for Zephyrine, but because the plant's parent company is a client, and the 'accident' would be filed through his own desk. He maps the insurance structure and finds the beneficiary: a trust with his old case number in its registration. Beat: dread becomes purpose.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She introduces Tomas Reiner, the chemist whose testimony the accident is designed to bury. Tomas is paranoid, brilliant, and refuses protection. Zephyrine's loyalty to him is the one thing she won't negotiate. Beat: the mission gains a human face—and a liability.

chapters.title: Someone Who Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A tail follows Emrys from work; he loses them using a route he doesn't remember learning. Confronting Zephyrine, he realizes she's been testing him—feeding him details of Marseille to see which ones he reacts to. Beat: trust inverted; neither can afford honesty yet.

chapters.title: The Safehouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Zephyrine stashes Emrys and Tomas in a derelict canal-side flat—her own safehouse, stripped and impersonal. Emrys recognizes the layout from a dream he's had for years. Beat: uncanny intimacy; the place feels like a memory he never made.

chapters.title: Aldous Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys confronts Vane, who admits he built Emrys's new identity six years ago—not to protect him, but as part of a witness-relocation deal Emrys himself brokered and then paid to forget. Beat: the floor gives way; Emrys chose this erasure.

chapters.title: What I Paid to Forget
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following Vane's ledger, Emrys reconstructs fragments: he was the conspirators' original architect, and he turned evidence, took the money, and bought oblivion. Zephyrine's 'favor' was invented by his own handlers as a loyalty leash. Beat: self-loathing—and the first real choice he's made in six years.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Someone tips off the conspirators to the safehouse. Zephyrine suspects Tomas, Tomas suspects Emrys, and Emrys realizes only Vane knew they'd be there. Beat: the circle tightens; loyalty fractures along every seam.

chapters.title: Canal at Midnight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. An attack team hits the safehouse. Zephyrine and Emrys escape with Tomas through the canal tunnels, but Zephyrine takes a graze wound and Emrys's cover identity is burned—his face is now on internal alerts. Beat: no way back; the run becomes the fight.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Hiding in a data center he once audited, Emrys uses his insider access to pull the accident's operational schedule: the 'gas leak' is set for the night before Zephyrine's extraction flight. He also finds the leak's signature—it's Vane. Beat: betrayal confirmed, clock running.

chapters.title: The Extraction Flight
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine reveals the dawn flight out of a private airfield—her exit, promised to Tomas. She offers Emrys a seat. He realizes accepting it means letting the plant burn and a stranger die in his place. Beat: the offer that costs everything to refuse.

chapters.title: Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys confronts Vane at his retirement cottage. Vane, dying, confesses he leaked the safehouse under coercion—his grandson's debts were the leverage—and gives Emrys the conspirators' internal verification protocol: the one credential that can halt the 'accident' is Emrys's own, presumed dead. Beat: the weapon is the self he buried.

chapters.title: Reactivation
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys walks back into his old firm as the man he used to be, using dormant credentials to flag the insurance claim as fraudulent and freeze the payout—the financial kill-switch that makes the accident pointless. Alarms trip everywhere. Beat: audacity; the invisible man becomes the loudest signal in the system.

chapters.title: The Plant
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The conspirators, unpaid and exposed, move the timeline up—tonight. Zephyrine and Emrys race to the plant to extract Tomas, who has gone there himself to photograph the tampered valves. Beat: chaos, courage, and the three of them finally trusting each other.

chapters.title: Dawn, Scheduled
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys confronts the operation's director in the plant's control room, trading the evidence ledger for Tomas's life while Zephyrine disables the valve release. The 'accident' is aborted minutes before ignition; the director is recorded confessing by the very compliance systems Emrys built. Beat: climax—truth deployed as a weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath of an Accident That Didn't Happen
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The story breaks: the fraud exposed, Tomas safe, Vane's coercion documented posthumously. Zephyrine's handlers want Emrys erased anyway—witnesses to the leash are liabilities. She burns her own extraction to shield him. Beat: loyalty chosen over survival.

chapters.title: The Empty Bag
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys unpacks the go-bag item by item—passport, cash, the lie he kept polished—and leaves it open on the bed. He files his real testimony under his real name, accepting prosecution risk and the end of his clean, invisible life. Beat: quiet, hard-won self-possession.

chapters.title: Zephyrine and the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Months later, Emrys—cleared, diminished, free—meets Zephyrine at the canal-side flat, which she's kept. Neither has a safehouse anymore; they have each other and an ordinary, dangerous honesty. The dawn flight leaves without them. Beat: belonging, finally, without a packed bag by the door.
